newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission seen blocking Anglo's Lonrho stake.
newsitem.headline: Commission seen blocking Anglo's Lonrho stake.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to block Anglo American Corp of South Africa's 28-percent stake in British conglomerate Lonrho Plc on Wednesday, European Union and industry sources said.

The Commission is likely to find that the stake gives Anglo American control of Lonrho's platinum division, a precious metal for which there is only another important producer in the world -- Gencor Ltd also of South Africa.

The decision was on the cards ever since the Commission banned a year ago the proposed merger of the platinum businesses of Gencor and Lonrho and European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert warned Anglo against increasing its shareholding in the British hotel and mining giant.
"I don't expect any last-minute surprise," an EU source said on Thursday after a meeting of senior Commission competition officials.
Anglo is still actively negotiating with the Commission, but the sources thought it would have to reduce its stake to a level where it would no longer have control of Lonrho.
Industry and anti-trust lawyers have speculated it could be nine or ten percent.
The excess could be put in a trust to be sold over a certain period of time, the exact duration of which would be known only by the Commission and Anglo.
Anglo American increased its stake in Lonrho from an initial 10 percent by acquiring 18.4 percent from Dieter Bock, a former Lonrho chairman, in November last year.
The Commission must vet all large mergers and acquisitions which affect trade in the EU.
